subject: Helios Analytics: Surge in token latency and elevated 5xx rate
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@heliosanalytics.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Helios Support <support@heliosanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: API latency spike across our tokenized pipeline

Marissa —

We started seeing a sharp increase in token latency around 08:45 PT and a corresponding rise in 5xx errors for our inference routes. Throughput is the same on our side (no higher QPS), but tail latency jumped to ~1.8s/token from ~0.6s/token and error rate reached ~3.5%. This is impacting real-time scoring in our production flows.

We tried switching to a fallback model you recommended last quarter but are seeing similar behavior. Can you confirm whether there are any ongoing infra events or config rollouts? We need an ETA for mitigation — our execs are asking for immediate visibility.

Attaching a short log excerpt and our trace IDs.

— Amit
Amit Shah
Head of Platform, Helios Analytics
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: API latency spike across our tokenized pipeline

Folks —

FYI: Helios (HLX-4231) just reported a sustained latency/5xx regression. They've attached trace IDs. Initial ask: confirm cause and provide short remediation/ETA.

Immediate requests:
- Jonas: can you start looking at serving cluster telemetry (GPU utilization, queue lengths, KV cache hit rate) for their region (us-west-2)?
- Neha: please assemble a minimal rollback/fallback plan (model variant + routing change + cache warm) we can push quickly if this is regression from a rollout.
- Laura/Vivek: I'll join customer comms once we have an initial diagnosis and an interim mitigation.

Priority: high — customer execs are engaged. Please add any additional folks you need.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: API latency spike across our tokenized pipeline

On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 09:23 AM marissa_cole@redwood.com wrote:
> Folks —
>
> FYI: Helios (HLX-4231) just reported a sustained latency/5xx regression.

Quick triage notes:
- I can see a sudden increase in inference queue length for the dedicated pool assigned to Helios starting 08:43 PT. GPU utilization is steady but queuing latency climbed.
- There was a background cache eviction job that ran at 08:40 PT in that pool (scheduled maintenance), which coincides with the start of the degradation. KV cache miss rate jumped from ~4% to ~48% immediately after.
- Error samples show a mix of model OOM retries and transient grpc timeouts (stack traces attached).

Immediate mitigation I can try now: pause the eviction job and rehydrate the cache from recent warm entries (may take ~8–12 min to reach steady-state). If that doesn't drop latency, we should fall back traffic to a warm model variant in a different pool.

I'll start the cache rehydrate and keep you posted.

— Jonas
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: API latency spike across our tokenized pipeline

Thanks Jonas — good catch.

Plan (steps, will update status inline):
1) Pause the scheduled eviction and kick off targeted rehydrate (Jonas) — ETA 12 mins.
2) If rehydrate fails to reduce tail latency below 1.0s/token within 15 mins, execute controlled traffic shift to the warm pool + enable KV-prefetch for Helios-only routes (~7–10 mins to ramp).
3) If errors persist after shift, perform a model rollback to the prior quantization profile (expected 20—30 mins including warm-up).
4) Customer comms: Laura will send an acknowledgement and a short, honest timeline; Marissa you escalate to Helios execs after we confirm step 1/2 results.

I've also asked infra to hold any disruptive jobs for the next 2 hours in us-west-2. If we need exec-level approvals for credits or SLA exceptions, flag now so I can pre-summarize.

— Neha
VP, Serving Runtime Ops
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@heliosanalytics.com>, Helios Support <support@heliosanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: API latency spike across our tokenized pipeline — initial update

Amit —

Thanks for the quick flag. We’re investigating root cause and have an engineering-led remediation in progress. Quick summary:
- Root candidate: scheduled cache eviction in your dedicated pool caused a jump in KV cache miss rate and increased queuing latency.
- Mitigation in flight: we paused eviction and are rehydrating cache now; this should reduce tail latency within ~10–15 minutes if effective.
- Next steps: if latency doesn't improve, we’ll route a subset of your traffic to a warm pool and enable KV-prefetch for your routes.

We’ll update you in 15 minutes with metrics and an ETA for full recovery. Apologies for the disruption — we know this affects your real-time scoring.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@heliosanalytics.com>, Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@heliosanalytics.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 18:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Helios operational summary and next steps (post-incident)

Amit / Priya —

Post mortem summary and current posture (final update):
- Timeline: incident began 2026-10-29 08:43 PT due to a scheduled cache eviction job that overlapped with increased cold-starts for Helios’ large-sequence requests.
- Impact: tail latency peaked at ~1.8s/token and 5xx rate reached 3.5% for ~22 minutes; throughput volume remained within normal bounds.
- Remediation: cache eviction paused; targeted rehydrate completed ~10 minutes after pause; selective traffic routing to a warm pool performed as a precaution and KV-prefetch enabled for Helios routes. Latency returned to baseline within ~25 minutes end-to-end.
- Root cause: insufficient coordination between scheduled maintenance window (eviction job) and dedicated-pool warm-up expectations for large-sequence workloads.
- Actions taken: updated runbook (attached), introduced pre-eviction warm checks, and added a safeguard to prevent eviction jobs on dedicated pools with active warm routes for 1 hour prior. We’ve also scheduled a joint runbook review with Helios engineering next week.

Compensation: Vivek and I will propose a goodwill credit to Helios for the customer impact; if you would like this to be escalated to Finance for formal approval, please let us know.

If you'd like a 30-minute post-incident call with our engineering and SRE leads, we can schedule for next week; otherwise, we'll send the joint runbook draft and the Grafana slices used in the investigation.

Appreciate your patience and partnership — we’ll follow up with the scheduled runbook review invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook-incident-checklist.pdf; helios_latency_trace_10-29.json; prod-error-sample-20261029.txt
